title: DiscoSign: Discourse-Aware Text to Sign Language Gloss Translation
gist: Apple and collaborators at Gallaudet and Northeastern argue that sign language translation systems fail because they operate sentence-by-sentence and ignore discourse structure; DiscoSign is a modular LLM framework that fixes spatial coreference, Question-Answer Clauses and concept-gloss consistency, plus a new evaluation metric suite because standard translation metrics cannot detect discourse-level quality. The raw record has no published_date field, though the page text states publication September 2026 at EMNLP.

themes.theme: Sentence-level processing as the root failure

insights.claim: Sign language processing systems have traditionally operated at the sentence level, ignoring discourse phenomena that are fundamental to how sign languages are actually comprehended.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Identifies a structural flaw shared by essentially every deployed sign translation product — a vendor still shipping sentence-level output is building on a known-broken unit of analysis.
insights.quote: Sign language processing systems have traditionally operated at the sentence level, ignoring critical discourse phenomena fundamental to sign language comprehension.
insights.locator: Sign language processing systems have traditionally operated

insights.claim: DiscoSign is presented as the first systematic framework for discourse-level text to sign language gloss translation together with a corresponding evaluation methodology, meaning the field had no established discourse-level baseline before it.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: First-mover framing in an accessibility sub-field with regulatory tailwinds; whoever sets the benchmark tends to set the procurement standard.
insights.quote: Our work establishes the first systematic framework for discourse-level text to sign language gloss translation with corresponding evaluation methodology.
insights.locator: Our work establishes the first systematic framework

themes.theme: Three discourse phenomena as the technical spec

insights.claim: DiscoSign targets three specific discourse phenomena: spatial coreference resolution, in which entities must maintain consistent spatial locations throughout a discourse; Question-Answer Clauses, which are pseudocleft structures serving specific discourse functions; and concept-gloss consistency, keeping stable mappings between English concepts and ASL signs.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A concrete, checkable spec for evaluating any sign-language AI vendor's claims — ask which of the three it handles.
insights.quote: spatial coreference resolution, where entities maintain consistent spatial locations throughout discourse
insights.locator: We address three key phenomena within our modular

insights.claim: The translation framework is modular and built on Large Language Models rather than a monolithic end-to-end sequence model, with linguistic research grounding each module.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Low-resource modalities are being solved by wrapping general LLMs in linguistically-informed modules, not by training bespoke models — cheaper to build, and it rides general LLM capability gains.
insights.quote: our modular Large Language Model (LLM)-based translation framework
insights.locator: We address three key phenomena within our modular

themes.theme: Evaluation metrics are the hidden bottleneck

insights.claim: Traditional translation metrics fail to capture discourse-level quality, so the authors had to introduce a suite of novel evaluation metrics designed to assess each dimension of discourse coherence their framework addresses.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Progress in this field has been partly invisible because the measuring instruments were wrong — expect published benchmark scores to be poor proxies for real usability.
insights.quote: Traditional translation metrics fail to capture discourse-level quality, so we introduce a suite of novel evaluation metrics
insights.locator: Traditional translation metrics fail to capture

insights.claim: Experiments on both sentence-level and discourse-level datasets show discourse-aware processing significantly improves spatial consistency and entity tracking relative to sentence-only translation while maintaining competitive single-sentence gloss translation quality.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The absence of a regression on single-sentence quality means discourse awareness is close to a free upgrade, so it should propagate quickly across the field.
insights.quote: significantly improves spatial consistency and entity tracking relative to sentence-only translation, while maintaining competitive single-sentence gloss translation quality
insights.locator: Experiments on sentence-level and discourse-level datasets

themes.theme: Annotated data as the binding constraint

insights.claim: AI-driven sign language interpretation is limited primarily by a lack of high-quality annotated data, and even new datasets containing professional interpreters and hundreds of hours of footage remain only partially annotated because annotating at that scale is prohibitively expensive.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The bottleneck is annotation cost, not model capability — value accrues to whoever industrializes cheap labeling, not to whoever has the biggest model.
insights.quote: New datasets including ASL STEM Wiki and FLEURS-ASL contain professional interpreters and 100s of hours of data but remain only partially annotated and thus underutilized, in part due to the prohibitive costs of annotating at this scale.
insights.locator: AI-driven sign language interpretation is limited

insights.claim: A companion Apple project attacks that cost directly with a pseudo-annotation pipeline that takes signed video plus English as input and outputs a ranked set of candidate annotations.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Watch for synthetic or model-generated annotation to unlock the existing unlabeled sign video corpus — the same unlock pattern that preceded step-changes in speech and vision.
insights.locator: In this work, we develop a pseudo-annotation pipeline

insights.claim: Current sign language generation systems fail to meet user needs for three concrete reasons: poor translation of grammatical structures, absence of facial cues and body language, and insufficient visual and motion fidelity.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A three-part failure checklist for due diligence on any avatar-based sign language product; fixing gloss translation alone leaves two of three gaps open.
insights.quote: poor translation of grammatical structures, the absence of facial cues and body language, and insufficient visual and motion fidelity
insights.locator: Sign languages are essential for the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing

insights.claim: The DiscoSign author list pairs Apple researchers with Gallaudet University — a Deaf-serving institution — and Northeastern University, with Gallaudet's contributors marked as having done the work while at Apple.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Credible accessibility work requires deep community-institution partnerships that are slow to replicate — a real barrier to entry for generic AI vendors entering this space.
insights.quote: § Gallaudet University** Work done while at Apple
